pillars.name: Governance
pillars.summary: Access control, auditability, accountability, and policies that keep the enterprise compliant without slowing teams down.

pillars.name: Application Security
pillars.summary: Shift-left security: secret scanning, dependency and code scanning, secure Actions, and a security-aware culture.

pillars.name: Architecture
pillars.summary: Scalable, resilient, observable platform design including runners, repository hygiene, and disaster recovery.

pillars.name: Collaboration
pillars.summary: Transparent ownership, discoverable repositories, and InnerSource practices that let teams work together.

pillars.name: Productivity
pillars.summary: Automation, AI-assisted development, engineering metrics, and feedback loops that accelerate delivery.

controls.title: Enterprise identity provider (SAML/OIDC) is configured
controls.description: Centralized identity through SAML SSO or OIDC (Enterprise Managed Users) ties GitHub access to your corporate identity lifecycle.
controls.remediation: Configure SAML SSO at the enterprise level (or adopt Enterprise Managed Users with OIDC) and pair it with SCIM provisioning so joiners, movers, and leavers are handled automatically.

controls.title: Two-factor authentication is required
controls.description: Requiring 2FA (or delegating it to an IdP) protects accounts from credential stuffing and phishing.
controls.remediation: Enable the enterprise policy that requires two-factor authentication for all organizations, or enforce MFA through your identity provider.

controls.title: Audit log streaming is configured
controls.description: Streaming the audit log to a SIEM or storage endpoint gives you retention beyond GitHub's defaults and enables alerting on unusual activity.
controls.remediation: Configure enterprise audit log streaming to your SIEM (Splunk, Azure Event Hubs, Datadog, S3, etc.) and build alerts for high-risk events.

controls.title: IP allow list is enabled
controls.description: Restricting access to known network ranges reduces the blast radius of leaked credentials.
controls.remediation: Enable the enterprise IP allow list (or your IdP's conditional access policy) for corporate network ranges and approved GitHub Apps.

controls.title: Base repository permission follows least privilege
controls.description: Organization base permissions of 'none' or 'read' avoid granting every member write or admin access to every repository.
controls.remediation: Set the base repository permission to 'No permission' or 'Read' and grant elevated access through teams.

controls.title: Members cannot create public repositories
controls.description: Preventing members from creating public repositories avoids accidental exposure of proprietary code.
controls.remediation: Disable public repository creation for members at the enterprise or organization level and provide a reviewed process for open-source publishing.

controls.title: Organization rulesets protect default branches
controls.description: Active organization rulesets that require pull requests on default branches enforce code review consistently across repositories.
controls.remediation: Create an active organization ruleset targeting ~DEFAULT_BRANCH across all repositories that requires pull requests and approving reviews.

controls.title: Rulesets require status checks
controls.description: Required status checks ensure CI and compliance checks pass before code merges.
controls.remediation: Add a 'Require status checks to pass' rule (or required workflows) to your organization rulesets.

controls.title: Custom properties categorize repositories
controls.description: Custom properties (e.g. owner, data classification, compliance scope) allow targeted policies and reporting at scale.
controls.remediation: Define organization custom properties for ownership and classification and use them to target rulesets and security configurations.

controls.title: Organization owner count is limited
controls.description: A small number of organization owners limits privileged access and makes accountability clear.
controls.remediation: Reduce organization owners to a small, named group and delegate day-to-day administration with custom organization roles.

controls.title: Periodic access reviews are performed
controls.question: Do you run periodic (e.g. quarterly) reviews of enterprise owners, organization owners, outside collaborators, and team membership, and remediate findings?
controls.remediation: Schedule recurring access reviews using audit log and membership exports; document and remediate discrepancies.

controls.title: Governance policies are documented and reviewed
controls.question: Are your GitHub governance policies (roles, repository standards, enterprise settings) documented, owned, and reviewed with stakeholders on a regular cadence?
controls.remediation: Publish a governance policy with named owners, a review cadence, and a feedback channel for developers.

controls.title: Backup and recovery procedures are tested
controls.question: Do you back up critical repositories and configuration (or GHES appliances) and regularly test restoration?
controls.remediation: Implement backups (GitHub Enterprise Server Backup Utilities or repository mirroring for GHEC) and run restore drills.

controls.title: Incident response covers GitHub access and policy violations
controls.question: Is there a documented, tested incident response procedure for compromised GitHub accounts, leaked tokens, or policy violations?
controls.remediation: Document runbooks for credential revocation, audit log investigation, and communication; test them through tabletop exercises.

controls.title: AI agents and Copilot usage are governed
controls.question: Do you have defined policies for Copilot features, coding agents, MCP servers, and AI credit budgets, with owners who review them?
controls.remediation: Define enterprise Copilot and agent policies, budgets, and an approval process for new AI capabilities.

controls.title: Secret scanning is enabled across repositories
controls.description: Secret scanning detects credentials committed to repositories.
controls.remediation: Apply a code security configuration that enables secret scanning for all repositories.

controls.title: Secret scanning push protection is enabled
controls.description: Push protection blocks secrets before they reach the repository.
controls.remediation: Enable push protection in your code security configuration and define a bypass review process.

controls.title: Dependabot security updates are enabled
controls.description: Automated security updates open pull requests to fix vulnerable dependencies.
controls.remediation: Enable Dependabot alerts and security updates through a code security configuration.

controls.title: Code scanning default setup is part of the security configuration
controls.description: Code scanning finds vulnerabilities in first-party code during development.
controls.remediation: Enable code scanning default setup in an organization code security configuration and apply it to all repositories.

controls.title: A default code security configuration applies to new repositories
controls.description: Default configurations ensure new repositories are secure by default.
controls.remediation: Mark a code security configuration as the default for new repositories in every organization.

controls.title: Critical and high Dependabot alert backlog is managed
controls.description: A growing backlog of open critical/high alerts signals vulnerability management is not keeping pace.
controls.remediation: Prioritize alerts using EPSS/severity, auto-triage rules, and security campaigns; set remediation SLAs.

controls.title: Open secret scanning alerts are remediated
controls.description: Open secret scanning alerts may represent live credentials.
controls.remediation: Revoke and rotate exposed secrets, then close alerts; track time-to-remediate.

controls.title: GitHub Actions usage is restricted to approved actions
controls.description: Allowing any marketplace action exposes workflows to supply-chain risk.
controls.remediation: Restrict allowed actions to GitHub-authored, verified creators, and an explicit allow list; pin actions to full SHAs.

controls.title: Default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions are read-only
controls.description: Read-only default workflow permissions limit the impact of compromised workflows.
controls.remediation: Set default workflow permissions to read-only and prevent Actions from approving pull requests.

controls.title: A security policy (SECURITY.md) is published
controls.description: A default SECURITY.md in the organization's .github repository tells people how to report vulnerabilities.
controls.remediation: Add SECURITY.md to each organization's .github repository so it applies to all repositories by default.

controls.title: Threat modeling is practiced
controls.question: Do teams perform threat modeling for critical applications and the software supply chain (including CI/CD)?
controls.remediation: Adopt a lightweight threat modeling process for new services and significant changes.

controls.title: Security champions and training program exists
controls.question: Is there a security champions network and recurring secure-coding training for developers?
controls.remediation: Establish security champions in each team and provide recurring secure-coding training tied to real alert data.

controls.title: Developer workspaces are secured
controls.question: Are developer environments (Codespaces, local machines, IDE extensions, tokens) governed with policies such as token expiration and approved extensions?
controls.remediation: Enforce fine-grained token policies, PAT expiration, and secure workspace baselines.

controls.title: Self-hosted runners are isolated with runner groups
controls.description: Runner groups scoped to specific repositories and blocked from public repositories prevent untrusted code from running on internal infrastructure.
controls.remediation: Organize self-hosted runners into runner groups with selected-repository visibility and disallow public repositories; prefer ephemeral runners (e.g. ARC).

controls.title: Inactive repositories are archived
controls.description: Stale, unarchived repositories add noise, cost, and security exposure.
controls.remediation: Archive repositories with no pushes in 12+ months after confirming with owners; automate the lifecycle with custom properties.

controls.title: Disaster recovery plan is documented and tested
controls.question: Do you have a documented disaster recovery plan for your GitHub platform and CI/CD (including RTO/RPO) that is tested at least annually?
controls.remediation: Define RTO/RPO for source control and CI/CD, document the plan, and test it on a schedule.

controls.title: Platform monitoring and alerting is in place
controls.question: Do you monitor GitHub platform health (runner capacity, Actions queue times, API rate limits, GHES appliance metrics) with alerting?
controls.remediation: Collect platform metrics (runner queue time, job failures, rate limits) into your observability stack with alert thresholds.

controls.title: CI/CD pipelines are designed for resilience
controls.question: Are CI/CD pipelines resilient to dependency outages (caching, mirrors, retries) and free of single points of failure?
controls.remediation: Add dependency caching/mirrors, retries, and redundant runner capacity to critical pipelines.

controls.title: Hosted runners use private networking where required
controls.question: Where workflows need private resources, do you use GitHub-hosted runners with private networking (Azure VNET) or equivalent controlled connectivity?
controls.remediation: Adopt hosted runner private networking or well-scoped self-hosted runners instead of opening inbound firewall rules.

controls.title: CODEOWNERS defines repository ownership
controls.description: CODEOWNERS files make ownership explicit and route reviews automatically.
controls.remediation: Add CODEOWNERS to active repositories and require code owner review in rulesets.

controls.title: Repositories are discoverable with descriptions
controls.description: Descriptions and topics make repositories discoverable for InnerSource reuse.
controls.remediation: Require descriptions (and topics or custom properties) for active repositories; report on gaps.

controls.title: Default community health files are provided
controls.description: A .github repository with CONTRIBUTING guidance sets consistent expectations across repositories.
controls.remediation: Create a .github repository in each organization with CONTRIBUTING.md, issue templates, and a profile README.

controls.title: InnerSource and champion programs exist
controls.question: Do you run an InnerSource or GitHub champions program that encourages cross-team contribution and shares best practices?
controls.remediation: Launch a champions program with clear roles, regular syncs, and recognition.

controls.title: Reusable workflows and shared assets are standardized
controls.question: Do teams share reusable workflows, templates, and actions from a central, versioned source?
controls.remediation: Publish reusable workflows and template repositories in a central location with versioning and ownership.

controls.title: GitHub Actions automation is adopted
controls.description: Repositories with CI workflows get faster, more consistent feedback.
controls.remediation: Provide starter workflows and reusable workflows so active repositories run CI on every pull request.

controls.title: GitHub Copilot seats are utilized
controls.description: Assigned Copilot seats that are active in the current billing cycle indicate healthy adoption.
controls.remediation: Run enablement for inactive seat holders, reclaim unused seats, and track adoption with Copilot metrics.

controls.title: Balanced engineering metrics are established
controls.question: Do you track balanced engineering system metrics (e.g. DORA, SPACE, developer experience surveys) and act on them?
controls.remediation: Choose balanced metrics across quality, velocity, and developer happiness; review them regularly.

controls.title: Developer feedback loop is closed
controls.question: Do you collect developer feedback on the platform and visibly act on it?
controls.remediation: Create feedback channels (surveys, discussions), publish outcomes, and integrate improvements into the platform roadmap.

controls.title: Continuous learning opportunities are provided
controls.question: Do developers have structured learning paths for GitHub, Actions, security, and Copilot?
controls.remediation: Provide learning paths, office hours, and certifications for GitHub features.
